Former site of Faraday Building Nth., City, Central, Long Distrance And International Telephone Exchanges 1902 - 1982

The Ferryman's seat located on previous buildings at this site was constructed for the convenience of Bankside watermen who operated ferrying services across the river. The seat's age is unknown but it is thought to have ancient origins.
Site of the Worshipful Company of Broderers Hall 1515 to 1940
On this site stood six successive Livery Halls of the Cordwainers' Company from 1440 until destruction of the sixth in 1941
Near this site in former times the Worshipful Company of Fruiterers had their Hall and warehouses and that "Fruiterers Alley" ran nearby [full inscription at https://openplaques.org/plaques/93790]

eras.label: Mapped site · auto T1
eras.summary: Location and terrain only. OpenStreetMap has no mapped outline for this site.
eras.basis: Everything drawn is traced from OpenStreetMap ways (ODbL) and the Terrarium elevation tiles. Each element names its OSM way.
eras.conjecture: Walls and buildings without a sourced height are drawn as kerb-high plan lines, never as masses. Closed walls have no gates: none are mapped. The DEM is ~30 m source resolution: it cannot show terraces, ditches or scarps. Nothing historic is depicted.

notes: site: osm:relation/10164871 historic=citywalls Q60308 789 m from ledger point
site is a site relation of 22 parts and none of them outlines the whole site, so no outline is drawn; the scene is fitted to the parts (1832 x 1208 m)
present-day buildings capped: kept the 60 nearest the outline centre of 389 mapped (trace size budget); the rest of the town is not drawn
roads capped: kept the 80 longest of 2017 mapped (trace size budget); minor lanes are not drawn
